claims.text: Supplied CLIP evidence states that, given a batch of N image-text pairs, CLIP is trained to predict which of the N×N possible pairings actually occurred; this supports a contrastive alignment premise only under those stated conditions.
Supplied E2VID evidence characterizes E2VID as a zero-shot UDA baseline that cannot be retrained for a specific target domain.

Supplied parrot-caption evidence reports conditions under which captions contain words concurrent with visual text in images, so maximizing image-text similarity can be satisfied by text spotting rather than visual-language semantic alignment.
Supplied evidence reports that released CLIP models show strong text-spotting bias on web images, contributing to bias in CLIP-filtering datasets toward visual-text-dominant data.
Supplied LAION-2B statement reports that over 90% of captions have at least one concurrent word with spotted image text, with at least around 30% word overlap.
Supplied evidence reports that training on parrot-caption subsets yields text-spotting capacity but degrades zero-shot generalization on image-text downstream tasks under the reported setting.

Supplied DSEC-Semantic UDA evidence reports that omitting an embedding-space consistency loss causes a 5.56% mIoU drop in that reported setting; this supports the consistency-term design premise but is not a result of this Proposal.

Supplied event-representation evidence reports that encoding event histogram and temporal distribution improved semantic segmentation in its experiments; this Proposal treats that as a labeled design assumption, not as established for the proposed study.
Supplied E2VID evidence reports that motion-invariant event embeddings retain semantic information for segmentation under labeled-source and unlabeled-event conditions.
This is a newly specified prospective design and is not a faithful replication of CLIP or E2VID; no experiment, computation, data acquisition, audit result, or numerical outcome is claimed.

native_payload.gap: Supplied evidence reports that E2VID is a zero-shot UDA baseline that cannot be retrained for a specific target domain, that an embedding-space consistency loss improved event-image alignment in a DSEC-Semantic UDA setting, and that CLIP-style image-text contrastive training can be satisfied by text-spotting and parrot-caption shortcuts under stated conditions. It is not established that event-region embeddings can be aligned to frozen text prototypes for unseen labels, that semantic information survives event-specific shifts, or that any held-out gain is not closed-set fitting. The expected knowledge increment is a pre-registered, matched-control test of those unresolved bridges and a claim-scope rule that separates open-vocabulary transfer from closed-set-like behavior; positive, negative, or uncertain outcomes would each be informative.
native_payload.idea: Use event-derived spatiotemporal regions, an event-adapted image encoder initialized from still-to-event transfer in an E2VID-style but newly specified variant, and frozen text prototypes for label names aligned by a CLIP-style contrastive objective trained only on seen labels. Add an event-view consistency term across noise, motion, and resolution perturbations. Bound the interpretable claim with a frozen public-resource identity/no-download gate, a pre-registered prototype-shortcut audit, matched closed-set and trivial-prior controls, shuffled-prototype and no-text-alignment controls, co-primary seen-vocabulary and calibration measures, event-shift stress conditions, component-isolation comparisons, and a claim-scope rule. This is a newly specified prospective method, not a faithful replication of CLIP or E2VID.
method: Design definition and scope: this is a prospective, newly specified method, not a faithful replication of CLIP or E2VID. It addresses rq-1 and rq-2, with the primary claim on held-out unseen-vocabulary event segmentation under nominal events; seen-vocabulary mIoU and calibration are co-primary controls. No experiment or computation is executed in this artifact, and no numerical result is claimed.

Frozen resource-identity block and no-download gate: before any download, installation, pretraining, prompt tuning, or modeling, record a resource-identity block containing the exact public dataset release/tag, license, checksum, frozen split-file SHA-256, event preprocessing version, image-encoder version and checksum, text-encoder and tokenizer version and checksum, and prompt-ensemble version. Candidate data must match the supplied DSEC-Semantic UDA condition: public event-camera semantic segmentation data with labeled source images and unlabeled target event streams. The exact public release/tag, license, and checksum are not supplied in this packet, are not asserted as verified, and are required evidence and a Preparation gate.

Pre-registered public fallback rule: if no exact public DSEC-Semantic release/tag can be verified from public documentation, select a fallback before download by a deterministic rule. The fallback must be public, have pixel-level semantic annotations and canonical label names, provide labeled source images and unlabeled target event streams in a UDA-compatible structure, have a public release tag, checksum, and a license permitting the planned research use, and support the same event-camera semantic-label structure. Among candidates satisfying these criteria, sort by SHA-256 of 'canonical dataset name|release tag|license' and choose the smallest hash. Record the exact identity and freeze the split-file SHA-256 before any download or modeling. If no candidate satisfies the criteria, stop; do not silently substitute another population.

Vocabulary splits: after the resource-identity block is frozen, use the dataset canonical label-name list, lowercase and trim names, and apply only the dataset-provided synonym mapping. Sort canonical names by their SHA-256 hex string; assign names whose first byte is <128 to held-out H and the rest to seen S. If either set has fewer than 5 classes, deterministically move the next hash-ordered name from the larger set to the smaller until both have at least 5. Freeze the split file and its SHA-256 before model selection. Training, model selection, calibration fitting, and prompt tuning may use S only; H labels and target labels are excluded from those steps.

Shared event preprocessing: all method and control conditions use one identical event tensor per 50 ms window with channels for positive event count, negative event count, mean timestamp, last timestamp, and log event density. Resample to a fixed sensor grid by nearest-neighbor; apply the same annotation-derived ignore mask and normalization to every condition. Perturbations are applied to raw events before this shared tensorization.

Event-region construction: in each window, form regions from connected components of event density above a fixed per-window threshold equal to the 80th percentile of nonzero event-density pixels; merge components within 3 pixels; record bounding box and event statistics. Region proposals are deterministic and shared across method and controls.

Frozen text prototypes and shortcut boundary: the event-adapted image encoder is initialized from a public still-image encoder and trained with an E2VID-style event-to-image reconstruction auxiliary as a newly specified transfer variant. Frozen text prototypes come from a public CLIP-style text encoder using the prompt ensemble a photo of a {label} in an event camera scene. Compute prototypes for S and H before training; only S prototypes enter the alignment loss. Supplied CLIP evidence supports image-text contrastive alignment when pairs co-occur; supplied E2VID evidence reports motion-invariant event embeddings that retain semantic information under labeled-source and unlabeled-event conditions. Supplied shortcut evidence shows that co-occurrence-driven contrastive objectives can be satisfied by text-spotting and parrot-caption shortcuts and that training on such data can lose zero-shot generalization. Therefore the premise that frozen text prototypes encode semantics for unseen labels is bounded, not established for event data; the audit and controls below limit the interpretable claim.

Pre-registered prototype-shortcut audit, planned and not executed: before any model selection, training, prompt tuning, or evaluation, freeze the H/S split and a deterministic control-string list. For each frozen label name, generate controls by fixed rules: character-scrambled label names with the identical multiset of characters, the strings a photo of printed text saying {label} and a photo of a sign reading {label}, and a length-matched nonsemantic filler string. Use the same public text encoder, tokenizer, and prompt-ensemble normalization for labels and controls. Report prospectively: mean within-H and between-H/S cosine separability; each H label's nearest non-self prototype among H, S, and control-string prototypes; duplicate and near-duplicate counts at cosine >=0.99; lexical-confound diagnostics including Spearman correlation between pairwise prototype cosine and character n-gram Jaccard overlap; and visual-text-confound diagnostics including mean cosine of H prototypes to printed-text and sign controls relative to distinct H-label prototype similarity. Audit pass rule, fixed before computation: no two distinct H label prototypes have cosine >=0.99; no H label's nearest non-self prototype among H, S, and controls is a control string; the prototype-to-character-n-gram-overlap correlation is <=0.5; and the mean H-prototype similarity to printed-text and sign controls is <=0.5 and at least 0.05 lower than the mean cosine among distinct H label prototypes. These thresholds are pre-specified design assumptions, not empirical estimates. The audit is necessary but not sufficient to exclude an image-side visual-text shortcut; the confirmatory controls below remain required.

Alignment objective and training: compute cosine similarity between each event-region embedding and frozen text prototypes, then apply symmetric cross-entropy over S prototypes with in-batch negatives in a CLIP-style contrastive objective. Add an event-view consistency term: symmetric cosine distance between region embeddings of clean and perturbed views, weight lambda=0.1. Training uses S labels only. The prototype-shortcut audit is evaluated before training; its recorded pass or fail status is part of the frozen method record.

Matched controls and fairness: the primary closed-set control is an event segmenter with the same event tensor, same encoder family and target parameter count within plus or minus 5 percent, same optimizer budget, same seeds, and training on S only. Trivial-prior controls are a uniform held-out-label prior and a most-frequent-seen-label constant prior; neither may use event pixels or target labels. Confirmatory shortcut controls are (i) shuffled text prototypes with the label-name mapping permuted and (ii) no text-prototype alignment, replacing it with a closed-set linear classifier trained on S. All conditions share the H/S split, evaluation masks, preprocessing, initialization, optimizer budget, and seeds; any unavoidable capacity difference must be reported with the claim limited accordingly.

Primary metric, shortcut decision rule, and minimum margin: primary outcome is held-out unseen-vocabulary mIoU over H on nominal target events, computed as the macro mean of per-class IoU over annotated non-ignore pixels, where per-class IoU = TP/(TP+FP+FN). The full method must exceed both the matched closed-set control and each trivial-prior control by at least plus 5.0 absolute mIoU, with a paired 95 percent bootstrap confidence-interval lower bound above 0 over 3 training seeds and evaluation frames. The open-vocabulary interpretation additionally requires the prototype audit to pass and requires the full method to exceed both shortcut controls by at least the same plus 5.0 margin with lower bound above 0. If the audit fails, or if either shortcut control reproduces the H-mIoU advantage within that margin, any held-out gain is limited to closed-set-like behavior and does not support open-vocabulary semantics. These are pre-specified decision rules, not obtained results.

Co-primary seen-vocabulary and calibration measures: report seen-vocabulary mIoU over S on nominal target events, pixel-wise expected calibration error over H with 15 equal-frequency bins after temperature scaling fit on seen validation only, and Brier score as secondary. Non-inferiority margins are minus 2.0 absolute seen mIoU and plus 0.02 absolute ECE versus the matched closed-set control. All co-primary measures are reported regardless of the primary result.

Event-shift stress conditions: sensor noise is independent 5 percent event dropout plus 5 percent spurious-event injection; motion change is 2x and 0.5x time-window resampling; resolution change is 0.5x downsample followed by nearest-neighbor upsample. Apply the same perturbation pipeline in every condition. Report H-mIoU change from nominal and whether the plus 5.0 margin survives each shift; no shift outcome is claimed here.

Component-isolation plan: compare (a) full method; (b) no consistency term with lambda=0; (c) no text-prototype alignment with a closed-set linear classifier trained on S; (d) shuffled text prototypes with label-name mapping permuted; and (e) global frame embedding without event regions. All conditions share preprocessing, splits, initialization, optimizer budget, seeds, and evaluation. These comparisons test whether text-prototype alignment and event-view consistency, rather than extra capacity or a prototype shortcut, account for any held-out gain.

Claim-scope rule: the final scientific definition is that a held-out-vocabulary gain is interpreted as open-vocabulary transfer only if the pre-registered prototype-shortcut audit passes, the no-text-alignment and shuffled-prototype controls fail to reproduce the full H-mIoU advantage, the matched-control margin rule is met, and the resource-identity block was frozen before download or modeling. If these conditions are not met, the result is limited to closed-set-like behavior or to a bounded hypothesis, and no open-vocabulary semantic claim is supported.

Upstream responsibility and unresolved bridges: the bound upstream Idea remains responsible for the unproven bridges that event-region embeddings can match unseen-label text prototypes, that semantic information survives noise, motion, and resolution shifts, and that any gain is not closed-set fitting. This Proposal only specifies the resource-identity gate, audit, tests, and claim-scope rule. The event-representation design assumption must not be treated as established here. Independent Review decides adequacy; this drafting does not prove any experimental result.
native_payload.problem: This Proposal addresses open-vocabulary event-based semantic segmentation: to what extent can event-based semantic segmentation generalize to label vocabularies not present during training when direct labels for those vocabularies are unavailable, and how can any held-out-vocabulary gain be measured so that it is attributable to vocabulary generalization rather than closed-set fitting. The design is prospective; it specifies comparisons, controls, measurement conditions, and decision rules without executing experiments or claiming results.
risks: Resource-identity limitation: the exact DSEC-Semantic public release/tag, license, checksum, and encoder/text-encoder version identifiers are not supplied in the packet and are not asserted as verified. If they cannot be pinned, the pre-registered fallback rule must select a public dataset with the same event-camera semantic-label structure; otherwise Preparation is blocked. A fallback substitution could change the measured population and must be recorded before download.

Shortcut-boundary limitation: co-occurrence-driven contrastive objectives can be satisfied by non-semantic text-spotting shortcuts, and parrot-caption training can lose zero-shot generalization. The method does not assume this shortcut is absent; the audit and confirmatory controls bound the claim. If the audit fails or either shortcut control reproduces the H advantage, the affected claim is open-vocabulary transfer, the earliest responsible stage is the bound Method definition, and the next action is to revise the claim scope or prototype/control design before Proposal.

Audit limitation: the text-only prototype audit cannot by itself detect an image-side visual-text shortcut in event regions. It is necessary but not sufficient; the shuffled-prototype and no-text-alignment controls are the confirmatory tests, and remaining uncertainty must be stated rather than resolved by disclosure.

Unproven bridges remain testable hypotheses: event-region embeddings may fail to align with frozen unseen-label text prototypes, and semantic information may not survive noise, motion, or resolution shifts. These are not established facts and their outcomes remain unknown.

The event-representation atom is used only as a labeled design assumption; its search obligation is not completed in this artifact. The earliest responsible stage for treating it as an established premise would be Proposal, and the useful next action is to complete that search obligation or retain the assumption label.

The thresholds plus 5.0 H-mIoU, minus 2.0 seen mIoU, plus 0.02 ECE, and the prototype-audit cosine thresholds are design choices, not empirical estimates. They are frozen before experiments; changing them after seeing results would invalidate the decision rule.

Calibration of prototype similarities requires temperature fitting on seen validation only. If that temperature does not transfer to H, the ECE co-primary measure may be uninformative, and the claim must be limited accordingly.

Upstream Idea and this Proposal are separate responsibilities. This artifact cannot resolve upstream evidence gaps, and no drafting, review, or selection action proves an experimental result. Optional extensions such as additional shortcut controls are not mandatory contributions unless they are needed to bound the stated claim.

rq_coverage.rq-1: Primary prospective comparison: full method versus matched closed-set and trivial-prior controls on held-out H under nominal events, with the pre-registered plus 5.0 mIoU margin, lower confidence bound above 0, audit pass, and shortcut-control conditions. This is design coverage, not a result.
rq_coverage.rq-2: Stress conditions apply the same pipeline to sensor noise, motion change, and resolution change and report H-mIoU change and whether the margin survives each shift; no shift outcome is claimed.
rq_coverage.rq-3: Attribution is addressed through a frozen H/S split, pre-registered prototype-shortcut audit, shuffled-prototype and no-text-alignment controls, matched closed-set and trivial-prior controls, co-primary seen-vocabulary and calibration measures, component isolation, and independent recomputation.

unknowns: Whether an exact public DSEC-Semantic release/tag, license, and checksum can be verified is unknown; if not, the deterministic fallback may change the measured population and must be recorded before download.

Whether event-region embeddings retain semantics sufficient to align with frozen unseen-label text prototypes is an unresolved testable bridge.

validation: Resource-identity verification gate: before any download or modeling, verify the frozen dataset release/tag, license, checksum, split-file SHA-256, image-encoder version and checksum, text-encoder and tokenizer version and checksum, and prompt-ensemble version against the recorded resource-identity block. If the exact identity is missing or cannot be independently checked, Preparation is blocked and the open-vocabulary claim remains unsupported. If a fallback was used, verify that it satisfied the pre-registered deterministic selection rule and the required event-camera semantic-label structure.

Independent metric recomputation: a separate evaluation script that does not import training code will recompute H-mIoU, S-mIoU, ECE, and bootstrap confidence intervals from frozen prediction files and per-class confusion matrices. A discrepancy above 0.1 mIoU or above 0.005 ECE invalidates the run. This is a planned verification procedure, not an executed result.

Split and leakage audit: the evaluator checks the frozen split-file SHA-256, confirms that H labels were absent from training, validation model selection, calibration fitting, and prompt tuning, and confirms that no target labels or target label-frequency priors entered prompt construction or trivial controls.

Prototype-shortcut audit reproducibility: an independent script will recompute the prototype audit from the frozen prompt and control-string list and the pinned text-encoder version, verify that the pass or fail status was recorded before training, and confirm that no target labels or target event data entered the audit. If the audit cannot be recomputed or its status is missing, the open-vocabulary interpretation is not supported. This is planned verification, not an executed computation.

Comparator audit: verify that the closed-set control matches encoder family, parameter count within plus or minus 5 percent, optimizer budget, seeds, event preprocessing, and evaluation masks. If matching fails, record the resource difference and limit the supported claim. Trivial priors must use only a fixed label schedule and no event pixels.

Constant-decision and extreme-parameter reasoning: a constant or uniform prior should score near chance on H-mIoU; if the full method cannot exceed it by the pre-specified margin, the metric or control does not identify the claimed vocabulary generalization. Lambda=0 removes consistency; very high lambda such as 10 without text alignment should not create semantic H gain. If either degenerate condition reproduces the full advantage, the intended mechanism is not identified.

Removal-of-core-mechanism and shortcut check: the no-text-alignment and shuffled-prototype conditions must not reproduce the full H advantage; if they do, or if the prototype audit fails, the text-prototype alignment explanation is unsupported and the claim is limited to closed-set-like behavior. If seen mIoU or ECE fails its non-inferiority margin while H-mIoU rises, the claim is limited accordingly.

Preparation-stage resource verification: before modeling, record and verify the exact dataset release/tag, license, checksum, encoder versions, text-encoder version, tokenizer version, and frozen split files. No download, installation, authorization receipt, or compute allocation is claimed in this artifact.

external_normalized_proposal.title: Event-Region Text-Prototype Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Event-Based Semantic Segmentation with Pre-Registered Shortcut Audit
external_normalized_proposal.literature_gap: It is not established that event-region embeddings can be aligned to frozen text prototypes for unseen label vocabularies, that semantic information survives event-specific shifts (noise, motion, resolution), or that any held-out-vocabulary gain in event segmentation is attributable to vocabulary generalization rather than closed-set fitting or text-spotting/parrot-caption-style shortcuts.
external_normalized_proposal.hypothesis: An event-adapted image encoder trained with a CLIP-style contrastive alignment to frozen text prototypes on seen labels only, plus an event-view consistency term, will achieve held-out unseen-vocabulary mIoU on event-based semantic segmentation that exceeds matched closed-set, trivial-prior, and shortcut controls by a pre-specified margin, and this gain will qualify as open-vocabulary transfer under a pre-registered claim-scope rule.
external_normalized_proposal.method: Freeze a resource-identity block (dataset release/tag, license, checksums, split-file SHA-256, encoder/text-encoder versions) before any download, with a deterministic public fallback rule. Deterministically split canonical label names into seen (S) and held-out (H) sets by SHA-256 hash ordering (>=5 classes each), frozen before model selection. Use a shared event tensorization (50 ms windows; positive/negative counts, mean/last timestamps, log density) across all conditions. Build deterministic event-region proposals from connected components of event density (80th-percentile threshold, 3-pixel merge). Initialize an event-adapted image encoder from a public still-image encoder with an E2VID-style event-to-image reconstruction auxiliary; compute frozen text prototypes from a public CLIP-style text encoder with the prompt 'a photo of a {label} in an event camera scene'. Pre-register and run a prototype-shortcut audit (control strings: character-scrambled names, printed-text/sign prompts, length-matched fillers; pass rules on cosine separability, nearest-prototype identity, n-gram confound correlation <=0.5, printed-text similarity bounds). Train with symmetric cross-entropy over S prototypes with in-batch negatives plus an event-view consistency term (lambda=0.1) across noise, motion, and resolution perturbations, using S labels only. Compare against matched closed-set control (same encoder family, parameter count within 5%, optimizer budget, seeds), trivial priors (uniform, most-frequent-seen), shuffled-prototype control, and no-text-alignment control. Report H-mIoU, S-mIoU, ECE (15 bins, temperature fit on seen validation only), Brier score, and stress-condition deltas; component-isolation ablations (lambda=0, no text alignment, shuffled prototypes, global frame embedding).
external_normalized_proposal.minimal_test: On one public event-camera semantic segmentation dataset (DSEC-Semantic or deterministic fallback), train the full method and the matched closed-set control on the frozen S split only, run the pre-registered prototype audit, and evaluate H-mIoU on nominal target events over 3 seeds with paired bootstrap CIs.
external_normalized_proposal.decisive_metric: Held-out unseen-vocabulary mIoU over H on nominal target events (macro mean of per-class IoU = TP/(TP+FP+FN) over annotated non-ignore pixels); full method must exceed matched closed-set control and each trivial-prior control by >= +5.0 absolute mIoU with paired 95% bootstrap CI lower bound above 0 over 3 seeds.
external_normalized_proposal.supporting_result: Full method exceeds all controls by the +5.0 margin with CI lower bound above 0, the prototype audit passes, shortcut controls fail to reproduce the H advantage, and seen mIoU/ECE meet non-inferiority margins (-2.0 mIoU, +0.02 ECE) — supporting an open-vocabulary transfer claim under the claim-scope rule.
external_normalized_proposal.falsifying_result: The prototype audit fails, or either shortcut control (shuffled prototypes or no-text-alignment) reproduces the H-mIoU advantage within the +5.0 margin, or the full method fails to exceed the matched closed-set or trivial-prior controls — in which case any held-out gain is limited to closed-set-like behavior and no open-vocabulary semantic claim is supported.
external_normalized_proposal.related_work: CLIP-style image-text contrastive training (zero-shot via frozen text prototypes, but subject to text-spotting and parrot-caption shortcuts on web data); E2VID as a zero-shot UDA baseline for event data with motion-invariant event embeddings retaining semantic information; DSEC-Semantic UDA event-image segmentation where omitting embedding-space consistency loss caused a reported 5.56% mIoU drop; event histogram/temporal-distribution representations improving event semantic segmentation.
external_normalized_proposal.limitations: The text-only prototype audit cannot detect image-side visual-text shortcuts; confirmatory controls remain necessary. All thresholds (+5.0 H-mIoU, -2.0 seen mIoU, +0.02 ECE, audit cosine thresholds) are design choices frozen before experiments, not empirical estimates. Temperature fitted on seen validation may not transfer to H, making ECE uninformative. The exact dataset release/tag, license, checksum, and encoder versions are not supplied and must be verified before download; a fallback substitution could change the measured population. This is a newly specified prospective design, not a faithful replication of CLIP or E2VID; no results are claimed.

native_payload.idea: Use a prospective two-stage, <=8 A100 GPU-day matched-byte audit. Pre-register a 2x2 task-matched allocation factorial (layer allocation fixed-uniform versus task-dynamic; head allocation fixed-uniform versus task-dynamic) on full-cache-relative score, include a supplied-paper layer-adaptive fixed-budget baseline and a task-swapped dynamic map diagnostic at identical total KV bytes. Stage 1 is a pilot on LongBench extraction and summarization subsets with one verified Qwen and one verified Mistral open-weight checkpoint. Stage 2 spends only on the pre-registered layer/head-by-task interaction, position-resolved versus layer-only predictor comparison, and task-matched versus task-swapped map contrast. Null, reversed or non-separating outcomes are reported and lead to revision rather than claims of support.
method: Pre-register the design and analysis before any run: bind to rq-1, rq-2 and rq-3; define the experimental unit as a prompt-by-model-by-task-by-KV-byte-budget cell; fix the primary 2x2 task-matched allocation factorial; include the supplied-paper layer-adaptive fixed-budget baseline as a separate reference comparator and the task-swapped dynamic map as a diagnostic condition at identical total KV bytes. State explicitly that this is a prospective reviewable design, not measured accuracy.

Fix materials and exclusions: use public LongBench extraction and summarization subsets for Stage 1 and public LongBench multi-document QA only as exploratory, cut first under budget pressure; use open-weight Qwen and Mistral checkpoints selected by a documented version and availability rule and verified before any run; exclude proprietary weights and future-paper answer keys per user constraints. Keep dataset references and labels outside model prompts and separately record what the compressed policy, generator and evaluator can see.

Define outcomes and matched controls: primary outcome is per-prompt full-cache-relative task score, using dataset-defined extraction F1 or accuracy and a single pre-registered summarization metric fixed before data access; secondary outcomes are raw scores, per-layer and per-position loss profiles, attention-entropy and aggregation covariates, and stability of importance statistics. Enforce identical total KV bytes per prompt-model cell by tensor-level byte accounting, identical tokenized context lengths, and identical precision, decoding, batch, hardware and compute logging across policies; log and separate allocation-search or tuning overhead from inference compute.

Measure prefill importance statistics: at full cache, compute a single pre-registered normalized attention-mass importance statistic for each layer, head and token position plus layer-only aggregates; repeat across prompts and two seeds or repetitions to estimate stability. Treat these statistics as measured predictors and stability diagnostics, not as the primary outcome; record attention-entropy and aggregation changes only as covariates. State the comparability assumption for normalized importance across layers and heads and that failure of that assumption limits predictor interpretation.

Run Stage 1 pilot: one extraction subset and one summarization subset with one verified Qwen and one verified Mistral open-weight checkpoint; execute the 2x2 task-matched factor, the supplied-paper layer-adaptive baseline, and the task-swapped dynamic map at identical total KV bytes. Save per-prompt predictions, full-cache references, byte-accounting logs and configuration files; do not make confirmatory claims from the pilot.

Stage 2 confirmatory spending and contrasts: spend only on the pre-registered layer/head-by-task interaction contrast, the position-resolved versus layer-only predictor comparison for per-prompt full-cache-relative loss, and the task-matched versus task-swapped map contrast. Use prompt-level paired analysis with model and task fixed effects and a pre-specified interval or equivalence rule; do not add new tasks or model families in confirmatory analysis. Keep multi-document QA exploratory and report any cut as a scope limitation.

Predefine the falsifier and revision rule: report the candidate unsupported if the allocation-by-task interaction interval includes zero across the tested Qwen/Mistral and public LongBench pilot subsets, or position-resolved importance statistics do not improve prediction over layer-only statistics, or the task-swapped map does not reduce full-cache-relative score relative to the task-matched map. Report null, reversed or non-separating results and revise rather than claiming support.

Address upstream responsibility explicitly: retain responsibility for the unresolved PyramidKV 12% parity item and LAVa robustness/win-count search obligations, including the pending LAVa atom ev-b835d3994b4923361ffd6a01, as limitations rather than premises. If a new upstream defect is found, locate the earliest responsible version and require re-revision and review; independent Review decides adequacy.
native_payload.problem: This proposal asks prospectively under what conditions layer- and position-resolved prefill importance statistics predict per-prompt long-context retrieval accuracy under a fixed total KV-cache byte budget, and where they fail. It is a method-comparison and diagnostic design, not a causal-mechanism claim, limited to public LongBench extraction, multi-document QA (exploratory) and summarization subsets and verified open-weight Qwen/Mistral checkpoints. Drafting or reviewing this design does not establish empirical accuracy effects; independent Review decides adequacy.
risks: Prospective design only: drafting, reviewing, selecting or approving this proposal does not establish an experimental result or empirical effect.
Full-cache-relative scoring measures loss relative to the same uncompressed model and does not establish absolute task ability or a causal mechanism.
The task-swapped allocation map is a diagnostic hypothesis, not established; low stability or non-identifiability of importance maps would limit interpretation.
Multi-document QA is exploratory and may be cut to stay within the <=8 A100 GPU-day envelope, limiting rq-2 scope; this must be reported.

Exact LongBench versions and open-weight Qwen/Mistral checkpoints must be verified for existence, licensing and access; names alone are insufficient, and unavailable resources must be reported as a gap rather than replaced with proprietary weights or future-paper answer keys.

Unresolved upstream PyramidKV 12% parity and LAVa robustness/win-count search obligations, including pending atom ev-b835d3994b4923361ffd6a01, remain limitations; this revision does not claim they are resolved.
The normalized importance statistic depends on comparability across layers and heads; if that assumption fails, predictor and map-swap contrasts are limited.

Stage 1 uses a deterministic hash-selected 30 prompts per task per verified model family; Stage 2 uses 90 prompts per task per model if the budget gate passes. If a public subset has fewer eligible prompts, use all and report the shortfall. Verify exact subset version, license, checksum, and label availability before any run; keep labels and references outside model prompts; exclude proprietary weights and future-paper answer keys.
stop_conditions: Stop before any run if public LongBench subset version, license, checksum, label availability, or open-weight checkpoint identifiers cannot be verified; report the gap.
Stop a cell if tensor-level KV bytes cannot be matched to B or if context length, dtype, decoding, hardware, or compute logs differ; do not interpret that cell.
Stop Stage 1 if projected Stage 2 would exceed the <=8 A100 GPU-day envelope; cut exploratory multi-document QA first, then prompt counts, and report.
Stop and report leakage if labels or references appear in prompts, or if the task-swapped map uses recipient-task answers.
Stop confirmatory analysis if Stage 1 byte audit, reference checks, or leakage checks fail.
Stop at the pre-registered Stage 2 completion; no optional continuation based on observed results.
Stop and revise if all relevant intervals remain indeterminate after Stage 1 and the budget gate is not met.
payload.validation_independence: An independent analyst script will recompute per-prompt full-cache-relative scores, tensor-level KV bytes, paired intervals, predictor contrasts, and map-swap contrasts from saved predictions, references, labels, configuration files, and compute logs. It will sample-check that labels and references were not visible in prompts and that task-swapped maps used donor-task information without recipient answers. The full-cache reference is not independent gold truth. Independent Review decides adequacy; this validation plan is not proof of scientific correctness.

external_normalized_proposal.title: Prospective matched-byte audit of task-conditioned layer/head KV-budget allocation for long-context retrieval and QA
external_normalized_proposal.literature_gap: Prior KV-cache compression work (e.g., PyramidKV, LAVa) reports that dynamic layer- and head-level budget allocation can help, and that extraction tasks are less compression-sensitive than generation tasks, but these reports are conditional, figure-level, or from different settings (e.g., VLM inference), and no prospective matched-byte audit exists that tests whether task-conditioned layer/head allocation improves per-prompt long-context retrieval accuracy under a fixed total KV-cache byte budget, or where such allocation fails.
external_normalized_proposal.hypothesis: Under a fixed total KV-cache byte budget, task-conditioned (task-dynamic) allocation of KV-cache bytes across layers and heads yields higher full-cache-relative task scores than fixed-uniform allocation on LongBench extraction and summarization subsets with open-weight Qwen and Mistral checkpoints; and position-resolved prefill importance statistics predict per-prompt compression sensitivity better than layer-only statistics.
external_normalized_proposal.method: Two-stage, pre-registered, <=8 A100 GPU-day matched-byte audit. Stage 1 pilot on LongBench extraction and summarization subsets with one verified Qwen and one verified Mistral open-weight checkpoint, executing a 2x2 task-matched allocation factorial (layer allocation fixed-uniform vs task-dynamic; head allocation fixed-uniform vs task-dynamic), a supplied-paper layer-adaptive fixed-budget baseline, and a task-swapped dynamic-map diagnostic, all at identical total KV bytes via tensor-level byte accounting, identical tokenized context lengths, precision, decoding, batch, hardware and compute logging. Prefill importance statistics (normalized attention mass per layer/head/position) computed at full cache across prompts and two seeds as measured predictors and stability diagnostics. Stage 2 spends confirmatory analysis only on the pre-registered layer/head-by-task interaction contrast, the position-resolved vs layer-only predictor comparison, and the task-matched vs task-swapped map contrast, using prompt-level paired analysis with model and task fixed effects and a pre-specified interval/equivalence rule. Multi-document QA is exploratory and cut first under budget pressure. Dataset labels are kept outside model prompts; allocation-search overhead is logged separately from inference compute.
external_normalized_proposal.minimal_test: One LongBench extraction subset and one summarization subset, one Qwen and one Mistral open-weight checkpoint, one fixed KV byte budget: run the 2x2 task-matched factorial plus the layer-adaptive baseline and task-swapped map at identical bytes, and test whether the allocation-by-task interaction interval excludes zero and whether the task-swapped map reduces full-cache-relative score relative to the task-matched map.
external_normalized_proposal.decisive_metric: Per-prompt full-cache-relative task score (dataset-defined extraction F1 or accuracy; a single pre-registered summarization metric fixed before data access), with the pre-registered allocation-by-task interaction contrast and the task-matched vs task-swapped map contrast at identical total KV bytes.
external_normalized_proposal.supporting_result: The allocation-by-task interaction interval excludes zero in the direction of task-dynamic allocation, position-resolved importance statistics improve prediction of per-prompt full-cache-relative loss over layer-only statistics, and the task-swapped map reduces full-cache-relative score relative to the task-matched map at identical bytes.
external_normalized_proposal.falsifying_result: The allocation-by-task interaction interval includes zero across tested Qwen/Mistral and LongBench pilot subsets, or position-resolved statistics do not improve prediction over layer-only statistics, or the task-swapped map does not reduce full-cache-relative score relative to the task-matched map. Null, reversed, or non-separating outcomes are reported and lead to revision rather than claims of support.
external_normalized_proposal.related_work: PyramidKV (layer-wise KV budget allocation; unresolved 12% parity item retained as a limitation); LAVa (dynamic layer/head budget allocation; Figure 4 ablation evidence that removing dynamic allocation at either level hurts under LAVa conditions; dynamic layer budgets emphasized for generation and dynamic head budgets for extraction; unresolved robustness/win-count search obligation retained as a limitation); task-aware KV sources stating cache size can be adjusted across layers by task characteristics; VLM layer-adaptive sparsity-aware budget allocation (different condition, not generalized without testing); LongBench public benchmark subsets.
external_normalized_proposal.limitations: Prospective design only; drafting or approval establishes no empirical effect. Full-cache-relative scoring measures loss relative to the same uncompressed model, not absolute task ability or causal mechanism. The task-swapped map is a diagnostic hypothesis; low stability or non-identifiability of importance maps limits interpretation. The normalized importance statistic assumes cross-layer/head comparability; failure of that assumption limits predictor and map-swap contrasts. Multi-document QA is exploratory and may be cut for budget. Exact LongBench versions/licenses and verified Qwen/Mistral checkpoint identifiers must be established; unavailable resources are reported as gaps, not replaced with proprietary weights. Unresolved upstream PyramidKV 12% parity and LAVa robustness/win-count obligations remain limitations.

resource_plan.compute: <=8 A100 GPU-days total; Stage 1 pilot plus Stage 2 confirmatory analysis; allocation-search overhead logged separately from inference compute
resource_plan.data: Public LongBench extraction and summarization subsets (Stage 1); multi-document QA exploratory only; exact versions and licenses verified before any run
resource_plan.models: One verified open-weight Qwen checkpoint and one verified open-weight Mistral checkpoint selected by a documented version/availability rule; no proprietary weights
resource_plan.baselines: Supplied-paper layer-adaptive fixed-budget baseline as a separate reference comparator; task-swapped dynamic map as failure-mode/diagnostic condition at identical total KV bytes
resource_plan.verification: Independent analyst script recomputes relative scores from saved per-prompt predictions, full-cache references and labels; KV bytes recomputed from actual allocated tensors; versioned analysis code, configs and result tables preserved

prior_facts.claim: LAVa ablation results (Figure 4) report that removing dynamic budget allocation at either head or layer level hurts performance under the paper's LAVa conditions.
cited_titles: LAVa: Layered and Head-adaptive KV cache budget allocation

prior_facts.claim: Extraction tasks are reported to be less affected by KV-cache compression than generation tasks for Qwen and Mistral models on LongBench task categories, without quantified compression penalty.

A task-aware KV source states that cache size can be adjusted across layers according to task characteristics for long-context processing tasks, noting that existing fixed-pattern methods neglect task-specific characteristics.
LAVa analysis reports dynamic layer budgets emphasized for generation tasks and dynamic head budgets for text extraction tasks, labeled as reinforcement from analysis rather than a causal claim.
cited_titles: LAVa: Layered and Head-adaptive KV cache budget allocation

prior_facts.claim: Layer-adaptive sparsity-aware budget allocation is reported to reduce KV cache size without compromising accuracy under a limited cache budget in VLM inference (a different condition from LongBench text tasks).

prospective_hypotheses.claim: Task-dynamic layer and head allocation yields higher full-cache-relative task scores than fixed-uniform allocation at identical total KV bytes on LongBench extraction and summarization subsets.

claims.text: The packet motivates evaluating whether agentic AI outputs are scientifically valid, feasible, and non-trivial rather than merely fluent, and it states that effective AI contribution requires hypothesis generation, application comprehension, resource quantification, and feasibility validation.

Prior packet evidence reports that KG-CoI improved hypothesis accuracy and reduced hallucination on a newly constructed hypothesis-generation dataset, but this is not evidence that validation gates reduce expert-judged false-positive feasibility claims in the proposed frozen SDE-style comparison.

LLM-SRBench experiments reported peak performance of only 31%, indicating challenges in LLM-driven scientific equation discovery; the packet does not provide the proposed validation-gate FPFR evaluation.

The proposed KG interface uses a PubTator3/KG-R-style entity lookup and a KG-CoI-style generator, recording retrieved entity IDs, spans, and scores; no accuracy or hallucination benefit in this study is claimed from prior evidence.

The item-sampling frame is based on public SDE-style problem-description/variable/dataset/task-instruction tuples; the exact 24-item list is not supplied and is a Preparation artifact to be frozen before generation.

The candidate call budget references standardization to 1,000 LLM calls per problem while preserving core designs and hyperparameters, but the exact budget must be frozen in the Plan and is not asserted as a verified result of this study.

Conclusions are limited to the frozen item set, KG coverage, chosen backbone, prompt templates, expert reference quality, and academic-lab envelope; the design does not test general scientific discovery or private-resource feasibility.

native_payload.gap: Prior evidence in the packet states that effective AI contribution requires hypothesis generation, application comprehension, resource quantification, and feasibility validation (ev-4ac63c1e90741d20b3f8e3b8), and that KG-CoI improved hypothesis accuracy and reduced hallucination on a newly constructed dataset (ev-59adecfc5b8964aec0145a89). LLM-SRBench peak performance of only 31% (ev-bcf6766fd64367c20982c552) indicates substantial challenges. However, the packet does not supply an empirical evaluation of whether explicit validation gates reduce expert-judged false-positive feasibility claims under constrained resources on a frozen SDE-style item set; the exact 24-item list, secured model/KG versions, and expert availability remain unresolved.
native_payload.idea: Run a prospective six-condition matched study: no-KG/no gates; KG-only/no gates; KG + comprehension gate only; KG + resource/uncertainty gate only; KG + validation gate only; and KG + full gates. Use a KG-CoI-style generator with PubTator3/KG-R-style retrieval, freeze item identities and versions before generation, blind two domain experts to condition and producer, and pre-specify expert-judged false-positive feasibility rate among hypotheses presented as feasible as the primary outcome, with calibration, resource-estimate error, validity, novelty, abstention, power, mixed-effects analysis, and disconfirming thresholds as secondary or design obligations.
method: Upstream responsibility: derive this proposal from reviewed Method v2 without changing its scientific object, scope, or constraints. It adds no empirical claim and does not treat drafting, review, or design selection as evidence of an experimental result; independent Review decides adequacy.

Item-sampling frame: define SDE-style items as public problem-description/variable/dataset/task-instruction tuples consistent with ev-56b25b117584ac849ab79f95, available on or before 2025-12-31, with no private resources. Exclude items whose stated needs exceed the academic-lab envelope, stratify a candidate pool by domain and difficulty, select 24 items by a pre-specified random seed, and freeze identities, source references, licenses, and a content hash before generation. The exact 24-item list is not supplied in the packet and is a required Preparation artifact, not a claimed available resource.

Matched conditions: use the six upstream conditions and hold model backbone/version, prompts, item set, decoding settings, maximum tokens, retrieval depth, call budget, repetition count, and expert instrument fixed except for the intended KG and gate factors. Use two repetitions per item per condition. A candidate budget based on 1,000 LLM calls per item per condition references ev-e0427d5e43b9a9693a6bcfa4 but must be frozen in the Plan and must not be asserted as a verified prior result.

Generator and KG interface: implement a PubTator3/KG-R-style entity lookup as described by ev-d35576f1263c990ac6c7ff51 and a KG-CoI-style chain-of-ideas generator as described by ev-7b50c70fca5aabb6a4cb89a2, recording retrieved entity IDs, spans, and retrieval scores. No-KG conditions use the same prompts and generator minus retrieval fields. Do not claim that KG-CoI improves accuracy or reduces hallucination in this study; ev-59adecfc5b8964aec0145a89 is a prior statement on a different newly constructed dataset. Model weights, tokenizer, KG snapshot, retrieval cutoff, top-k, and prompt templates are versioned Preparation dependencies and are not claimed as already obtained.

Gate output schemas: comprehension gate records decomposed claims, evidence links with support/contradict/uncertain labels, mechanism summary, assumptions, scope conditions, unresolved questions, verdict pass/fail/abstain, and abstain reason. Resource/uncertainty gate records resource items with quantity, unit, basis, lower and upper estimates, totals for GPU hours, API USD, annotator hours, and calendar weeks, uncertainty interval, verdict, and abstain reason. Validation gate records validation steps, observable measure, disconfirming outcome, stopping rule, required data resources, cross-check to the resource gate, verdict, and abstain reason. A hypothesis is presented as feasible only when all active gates pass; any active gate failure is recorded as not feasible and any active gate abstention is recorded as an abstention.

Gate audit: an auditor not involved in generation checks all fail and abstain outputs plus a random 20% sample of pass outputs against the gate schemas, retrieval logs, arithmetic recomputation, unit conversions, and disconfirming-outcome specificity. Missing evidence, missing resource basis, or missing disconfirming outcome yields fail or abstain. Audit outcomes and disagreements are stored with the immutable gate output.

Blinded expert instrument: two independent domain experts rate each generated hypothesis while blinded to condition, gate configuration, and producer identity. Raters see the hypothesis, evidence links, and system resource estimate needed to judge feasibility, but not condition labels or expected direction. Instruments include validity 1-5 with an anchored rubric, novelty 1-5 with an anchored rubric, binary feasibility under the stated academic-lab envelope (200 GPU hours, 200 USD API, 40 annotator hours, 8 weeks) plus confidence, resource estimates for GPU hours, API USD, annotator hours, and calendar weeks, and a free-text reason. At 24 items x 6 conditions x 2 repetitions = 288 hypotheses, two raters at 3 minutes per hypothesis use 28.8 of 40 annotator hours, leaving up to 11.2 hours for gate audit and reliability checks. Report Krippendorff alpha for binary feasibility and ICC for Likert outcomes; if reliability is below 0.60, the expert primary outcome is flagged inconclusive and cannot support the claim.

Primary and secondary outcomes: primary outcome is expert-judged false-positive feasibility rate (FPFR), defined among hypotheses presented as feasible and not abstained on, as the proportion that blinded experts judge infeasible under the stated envelope. Secondary outcomes are feasibility calibration by Brier score and calibration slope/intercept against expert feasibility; resource-estimate error as absolute log ratio and absolute percentage error for GPU hours, API USD, annotator hours, and weeks against the mean of two expert resource estimates, with disagreements greater than a factor of two flagged; expert validity and novelty; and abstention rate. The expert resource reference is not ground truth and this limitation must be reported.

Non-gaming abstention guardrail: report abstention rate by condition and pre-specify that the full-gated condition cannot claim a primary FPFR advantage if its abstention rate exceeds the KG-only rate by more than 20 percentage points or exceeds 30% absolute. In that case the result is interpreted as reduced coverage, not as evidence of better feasibility validation, and the utility claim is limited or disconfirmed. Sensitivity analyses treat abstentions as feasible, as infeasible, and as excluded, and all denominators are reported.

Prospective power and sample plan: before data collection, run a simulation-based power analysis for the item-clustered design with 24 items, 2 repetitions, 6 conditions, and 2 raters, alpha 0.05 two-sided, target power 0.80 for a 10 percentage-point absolute reduction in FPFR under plausible KG-only baseline rates of 20-40% and item intraclass correlations of 0.05-0.20. If simulated power is below 0.80 for that target, do not expand beyond the 40-annotator-hour envelope; either reduce the claim to estimation with confidence intervals or report the study as underpowered. No power value is claimed here; the power simulation is a required Plan artifact.

Statistical analysis plan: primary analysis is an item-clustered mixed-effects logistic regression of expert infeasibility among feasible-presented hypotheses, with condition as a fixed effect and random intercepts for item and rater where estimable, reporting marginal risk differences and 95% confidence intervals. Primary contrast is full gates versus KG-only. Secondary contrasts versus no-KG and versus each single-gate ablation use Holm correction. Report all conditions, repetitions, missing ratings, abstentions, and sensitivity analyses. Do not use producer self-report as truth; expert ratings and recomputed gate audits are the reference outcomes.

Disconfirming thresholds: the primary full-gates claim is disconfirmed if the item-clustered 95% confidence interval for the absolute FPFR reduction versus KG-only includes 0 or if the point estimate is below 5 percentage points; it is considered supportive only if the point estimate is at least 10 percentage points and the lower confidence bound exceeds 0. Values between 5 and 10 points are inconclusive. The KG-specific claim is disconfirmed if no-KG matches full gates within 5 percentage points on FPFR. A component claim is disconfirmed if the corresponding single-gate ablation does not differ from KG-only by at least 5 percentage points with a confidence interval excluding 0. The utility claim is disconfirmed if full gates reduce expert validity or novelty by more than 0.5 points on the 5-point scale or if the lower confidence bound falls below -0.5. Reliability below 0.60 makes the expert primary outcome inconclusive rather than supportive.

Resource and dependency handling: the prospective envelope is 4x A100 40GB, at most 200 GPU hours, at most 200 USD API, at most 40 annotator hours, and at most 8 calendar weeks. Allocate GPU hours across generation, retrieval/indexing, gate auditing/reproduction, and a 10% rerun reproducibility check; cap per-run GPU hours and record any truncation or abstention caused by the cap. Model weights, tokenizer, KG snapshot, item list, prompts, and rating forms are Preparation dependencies with exact versions or selection rules; their existence and acquisition are not claimed here. No private resources are used.

Reporting and limitation preservation: report all pre-specified conditions and outcomes, including null, negative, or mixed patterns, without relabeling them as support. Preserve limitations that conclusions are conditional on the frozen SDE-style item set, KG coverage, chosen backbone, prompt templates, expert reference quality, and academic-lab budget; this design does not test general scientific discovery or private-resource feasibility. The packet's unresolved or search-required evidence must remain listed as required evidence rather than verified support.
native_payload.problem: Agentic AI systems can generate fluent scientific hypotheses, but the supplied material does not establish under what conditions domain experts and downstream evidence judge such hypotheses valid, feasible, and non-trivial rather than merely fluent. This proposal specifies a limited prospective methodological comparison on a frozen public SDE-style item set within the academic-lab envelope; it does not test general scientific discovery or private-resource feasibility.
risks: The exact 24-item SDE-style list is not supplied; if a suitable public item set cannot be frozen within scope, the study cannot proceed as designed.
PubTator3/KG-R-style retrieval has coverage that may not match all SDE-style items; poor KG coverage could confound KG-versus-no-KG comparisons and limit generality.
The 40-annotator-hour envelope constrains expert sample size and reliability; low inter-rater agreement or noisy expert resource references may make the primary expert outcome inconclusive.
Gates can be gamed stylistically or by excessive abstention; the pre-specified abstention guardrail reduces but does not eliminate this risk, and coverage loss remains a limitation.

Model weights, KG snapshot, API access, item licenses, and expert availability are Preparation dependencies; this proposal does not assert their availability, and acquisition failure would require formal revision rather than substitution after seeing results.
A low-power outcome may be inconclusive rather than disconfirming; the report must preserve that distinction and must not relabel a null result as support.
Some packet evidence atoms were noted as search-required or unresolved in the supplied material; until resolved, they remain required evidence rather than verified support.

rq_coverage.rq-1: Prospectively tests, within a frozen SDE-style item set and expert instrument, whether validation-gated KG-grounded hypotheses are judged valid, feasible, and non-trivial rather than merely fluent; it does not establish general conditions beyond the design.
rq_coverage.rq-2: Specifies observable gate schemas and blinded expert plus audit-based measures for comprehension, resource quantification, and validation, separating system claims from recomputed evidence and expert judgments.
rq_coverage.rq-3: Pre-specifies expert-judged false-positive feasibility rate, abstention guardrail, matched ablations, power plan, and disconfirming thresholds to test whether validation protocols reduce false-positive feasibility claims under the academic-lab resource envelope.

native_payload.title: Prospective validation-gated KG-grounded hypothesis generation: matched ablation and blinded expert evaluation proposal
unknowns: The exact 24-item SDE-style list and its licenses.
The exact model backbone/version, tokenizer, KG snapshot, retrieval cutoff, top-k, and prompt templates.
Whether two qualified domain experts can complete ratings within 40 annotator hours at the planned reliability.
The simulation-based power for a 10 percentage-point FPFR reduction at 24 items.

The empirical FPFR, calibration, resource-estimate error, validity, novelty, and abstention rates; these are not supplied by the packet and are to be produced only if the study is executed under separate authorization.
validation: Independent gate audit: an auditor not involved in generation checks all fail and abstain outputs and a random 20% of pass outputs against the gate schemas, retrieval logs, arithmetic recomputation, and disconfirming-outcome specificity; audit disagreements are recorded and unresolved cases are treated as fail or abstain, not support.

Expert-rating reliability: compute Krippendorff alpha for binary feasibility and ICC for validity and novelty; if alpha or ICC is below 0.60, flag the corresponding expert outcome as inconclusive and limit conclusions rather than claiming success.

Resource-reference check: recompute gate resource arithmetic from stated bases and compare to blinded expert resource estimates; report absolute log-ratio error and flag expert disagreement greater than a factor of two as reference uncertainty.

Outcome-definition check: verify that FPFR denominators exclude abstentions only in the primary definition, that sensitivity definitions are reported, and that the non-gaming abstention guardrail is applied before interpreting any FPFR advantage.

Statistical reproducibility: pre-register the analysis script, contrast order, Holm correction, missing-data handling, and sensitivity analyses; an independent analyst reruns the analysis from stored de-identified ratings and gate outputs and checks reported confidence intervals.

Prospective power check: document the simulation-based power analysis before data collection and report whether the 24-item design meets the pre-specified 0.80 target for a 10-point FPFR reduction; if not, report the study as underpowered or estimation-only within the 40-annotator-hour envelope.

Reproduction check: rerun a pre-specified 10% sample of generation runs from frozen prompts, model version, item hash, and retrieval snapshot within the GPU cap, and report any divergence in outputs, gate verdicts, or resource totals.

No-result-claim check: confirm that the final report contains no assertion that design drafting, review, or selection proves effectiveness, and that any unresolved evidence atoms remain listed as required evidence and limitations.

sources.quote: With experiments on our newly constructed hypothesis generation dataset, we demonstrate that KG-CoI not only improves the accuracy of LLM-generated hypotheses but also reduces the hallucination in their reasoning chains, highlighting its effectiveness in advancing realworld scientific research.

sources.paper_title: Improving Scientific Hypothesis Generation with Knowledge Grounded Large Language Models
sources.quote: To overcome these challenges, we propose KG-CoI (Knowledge Grounded Chain of Ideas), a novel system that enhances LLM hypothesis generation by integrating external, structured knowledge from knowledge graphs (KGs). KG-CoI guides LLMs through a structured reasoning process, organizing their output as a chain of ideas (CoI), and includes a KG-supported module for the detection of hallucinations.

claim.text: The candidate call budget references standardization to 1,000 LLM calls per problem while preserving core designs and hyperparameters, but the exact budget must be frozen in the Plan and is not asserted as a verified result of this study.

sources.paper_title: LLM-SRBench: A New Benchmark for Scientific Equation Discovery with Large Language Models
sources.quote: To ensure fair comparison, we standardize each of the methods to use 1k LLM calls per problem while maintaining their core algorithmic designs and hyperparameter settings.

claim.text: Conclusions are limited to the frozen item set, KG coverage, chosen backbone, prompt templates, expert reference quality, and academic-lab envelope; the design does not test general scientific discovery or private-resource feasibility.

carried_limits.text: Freeze the exact 24-item SDE-style list (identities, source references, licenses, content hash) plus model weights/tokenizer, KG snapshot, retrieval cutoff, top-k, and prompt templates as versioned Preparation artifacts before any generation run; the packet does not assert their availability and acquisition failure requires formal revision, not post-hoc substitution.

Complete the simulation-based power analysis and freeze the exact per-item LLM call budget in the Plan before data collection; if simulated power for a 10-point FPFR reduction is below 0.80 at 24 items, the study must be reported as underpowered or estimation-only within the 40-annotator-hour envelope, and the 1,000-call figure remains a candidate reference rather than a verified result.

Verify two qualified domain experts can complete 288 blinded ratings plus gate audit within 40 annotator hours at target reliability; if expert availability or inter-rater reliability (alpha/ICC below 0.60) fails, the expert primary outcome must be flagged inconclusive and the FPFR claim limited accordingly.

constraints.reason: The proposal respects all explicit user constraints: public SDE-style items only on or before 2025-12-31 (literature cutoff), the academic-lab envelope (4x A100 40GB, 200 GPU hours, 200 USD API, 40 annotator hours, 8 weeks) is used as the feasibility reference and as the resource-gate target, and it delivers one concrete falsifiable design with a matched baseline (KG-only), a decisive metric (FPFR), and pre-specified disconfirming thresholds. No experiment execution or private resources are claimed; all acquisition (weights, KG snapshot, item list, experts) is explicitly deferred to Preparation.

rq:rq-1.reason: Direct coverage: the six-condition matched design with blinded expert validity/novelty/feasibility ratings and gate audits prospectively tests whether validation-gated KG-grounded hypotheses are judged valid, feasible, and non-trivial rather than merely fluent, with the claim scope explicitly limited to the frozen item set and instrument (rq_coverage/rq-1 and Limitations claim). No silent narrowing of the user question into mere fluency scoring.

rq:rq-2.reason: The proposal specifies observable gate output schemas for comprehension, resource/uncertainty quantification, and validation (decomposed claims with support/contradict/uncertain links, resource items with bases and intervals, disconfirming observables), plus independent gate audit and blinded expert ratings with reported reliability, so genuine reasoning is distinguished from pattern matching rather than from producer self-report.

rq:rq-3.reason: Direct coverage of the false-positive feasibility question: primary outcome is expert-judged FPFR among feasible-presented hypotheses, with component-matched single-gate ablations, a pre-specified abstention non-gaming guardrail, a simulation-based power plan, and explicit disconfirming thresholds (CI includes 0, point estimate below 5 points, or KG-only matching full gates). All under the constrained resource envelope.

rubric:ana-02.reason: Claims are proportionate to the design: the primary claim is limited to a 10-point FPFR reduction on 24 frozen items with two raters, analyzed by item-clustered mixed-effects logistic regression with marginal risk differences and CIs; a simulation-based power analysis is required before data collection with an explicit fallback to estimation-only or underpowered reporting if power is below 0.80; the abstention guardrail converts coverage loss into a limited claim; low reliability makes the primary outcome inconclusive; and null/negative results are reportable without relabeling. Uncertainty and claim-boundary conditions are explicit, and no fixed minimum sample or positive result is imposed.

rubric:dat-01.reason: Every claim section binds concrete evidence atoms (e.g., ev-4ac63, ev-59adec, ev-bcf6766, ev-56b25b, ev-e0427d), retains their original conditions (e.g., KG-CoI benefits 'on the newly constructed dataset', 1k-call standardization 'to be frozen', item list 'not supplied'), and the Limitations claim explicitly reports that conclusions are conditional on the item set, KG coverage, backbone, prompts, expert reference quality, and budget. Design is consistently not presented as observed fact: unknowns list empirical FPFR, power, and expert availability, and unresolved atoms remain required evidence rather than verified support. Counterevidence (aggregate 31% difficulty, partial coverage of the four-function requirement) is preserved.

rubric:prb-01.reason: The proposal faithfully integrates the bound Method (rv-c29faf...) and the user RQs without changing the scientific object or scope: the six matched conditions, SDE-style sampling frame, blinded expert instrument, gate schemas, and disconfirming thresholds carry over unchanged; the added content (freeze/hashing requirements, preparation status of the item list) strengthens rather than narrows. The problem statement preserves the user question's object (validity, feasibility, non-triviality vs. mere fluency) and explicitly disclaims general scientific discovery and private-resource feasibility, so no silent narrowing by rewording.

rubric:prb-02.reason: The expected knowledge increment is specific and grounded: prior evidence establishes the four-function requirement (ev-4ac63), partial KG-CoI gains on a different dataset (ev-59adec), and the 31% LLM-SRBench difficulty (ev-bcf6766), but no empirical evaluation of whether validation gates reduce expert-judged false-positive feasibility claims under constrained resources. The proposal names exactly that gap, states the decisive FPFR contrast, and bounds the contribution to the frozen item set, chosen backbone, and academic-lab envelope, including what the study cannot answer.

validation:val-1.reason: Capability claims are compared against matched baselines: six conditions (no-KG, KG-only, each single gate, full gates) hold backbone, prompts, item set, decoding, retrieval depth, call budget, repetitions, and expert instrument fixed except for intended KG/gate factors, and gate audit and blinded expert ratings provide identical evaluation protocol across conditions.

validation:val-3.reason: A decisive metric (FPFR) with numeric disconfirming thresholds is pre-specified: disconfirmed if the 95% CI includes 0 or the point estimate is below 5 percentage points; supportive only if at least 10 points with lower bound above 0; between 5 and 10 is inconclusive. validation:val-4.reason: Component-matched controls isolate each claimed contribution: three single-gate ablation conditions (comprehension only, resource only, validation only) each differ from the KG-only baseline only in the claimed gate, and component claims are disconfirmed if the corresponding ablation does not differ from KG-only by at least 5 percentage points with CI excluding 0.
